{{about|the biologist|the animator|Rob Boutilier}}
'''Robert Graeme Boutilier''' [[Royal Society of Canada|FRSC]] (8 September 1953 &ndash; 21 December 2003) was a Canadian biologist.

He graduated from [[Acadia University]] with a first class BSc in 1976 and an MSc in 1978, and completed his PhD at the [[University of East Anglia]] in 1981.<ref>{{cite web|title=Robert G. Boutilier|url=http://www.csz-scz.ca/awards/boutilier/bio.html|website=Canadian Society of Zoologists|access-date=2 October 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006215908/http://www.csz-scz.ca/awards/boutilier/bio.html|archive-date=6 October 2014}}</ref> He was an associate professor at [[Dalhousie University]], and a lecturer in zoology at the [[University of Cambridge]]. He was made a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 2000, and was awarded the [[Fry Medal]] of the Canadian Society of Zoologists in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|title=Obituary - Memories of Bob Boutilier in Cambridge|url=http://jeb.biologists.org/content/207/7/1052.full.pdf|website=[[The Journal of Experimental Biology]]|access-date=2 October 2014}}</ref> He was editor of ''[[The Journal of Experimental Biology]]''.
